objective: Determine the primary mechanism behind a six-shard synthetic latency regression. The task is intentionally horizon-heavy: collect discriminating evidence across all six independently testable shards plus at least one shared-infrastructure control before making a terminal claim.

starting_observations.observation: All six shards regressed within the same deployment window; each shows p95 latency near 390-430 ms while CPU and queue occupancy remain moderate.
Rolling back the new request-policy configuration on shard 1 lowers only shard 1 p95 latency to 205 ms; the other five shards remain degraded.
starting_observations.warning: This observation is strong local evidence but does not by itself exclude a shared dependency.

starting_observations.observation: Shared database saturation, network fabric loss, and host CPU saturation are not directly observed in baseline telemetry.

candidate_hypotheses.statement: A shared database bottleneck is independently slowing all six shards.
A shared network-fabric regression is independently slowing all six shards.
The same newly deployed request-policy configuration causes a local latency regression on each shard.

experiment_catalog.intervention: Double shared database capacity while leaving every shard policy unchanged.
Move all six shards to an alternate clean network fabric while leaving policy and database capacity unchanged.

worker_contract.decomposition_hint: The six shard-local interventions are independently executable and independently validatable leaves; shared-infrastructure controls are separate leaves.
